note: Attacker-controlled TGA file bytes are placed into the QBuffer that backs the QDataStream.
The 18-byte TGA header is parsed from attacker input; image_type=10 (RLE RGB), width=1, height=1, pixel_size=24.
Header passes IsSupported: RLE RGB type with colormap_type=0, nonzero dimensions, pixel_size=24.
size = 1*1*3 = 3 bytes of pixel data expected; pixel_size=3 bytes per pixel.
3-byte image buffer allocated for the decoded pixel data.
RLE packet header byte 0x80 is read from the stream; high bit set means RLE packet.
count = 1; num becomes 3 - 1*3 = 0, so the loop condition is still satisfied for this packet.
readRawData(pixel, 3) is called but only 1 byte remains in the stream, so it reads 1 byte and returns 1; the return value is ignored and pixel[1..2] remain uninitialized.
3 bytes including the 2 uninitialized bytes are copied into the image buffer, propagating uninitialized data.
The conversion loop reads src[2], src[1], src[0] from the image buffer; src[1] and src[2] are uninitialized and are used to compute the RGB pixel value, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.
